target.title: fix(imessage): plain-send fallback for threaded replies + db-scoped recovery cursor (#99638)
target.body:
Closes #99638

## What Problem This Solves

Issue #99638 reported three failures on the dedicated bot-user / SSH-wrapped iMessage deployment. The primary one (every DM after the first failing with `reply session initialization conflicted`) was already fixed by #98835. This PR fixes the two remaining reported failures:

- **Threaded replies were dropped on AppleScript-only deployments.** When a reply payload carried `reply_to` but the private-API bridge was unavailable, `imsg` hard-errored (`reply_to requires bridge transport; ...`) and OpenClaw rethrew, so the reply was **lost** with no fallback.
- **Repointing `dbPath` silently stopped all inbound.** The downtime-recovery cursor was keyed per account, not per database, and is monotonic. After pointing `dbPath` at a different `chat.db` with lower rowids (e.g. a fresh bot-user DB, max rowid ~15), the stale high-water (~12396) was still sent as `since_rowid`, so `imsg` replayed/emitted nothing and inbound was **silently lost forever**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both fixes stay entirely within `extensions/imessage` (no core or config-surface changes):

- **Plain-send fallback (`send.ts`):** the send `catch` now detects the specific "threaded reply unsupported" error and, when a `reply_to` was set, retries the send once with `reply_to` stripped — delivering the message unthreaded instead of dropping it. The match is a closed error class, so unrelated send failures still propagate.
- **DB-scoped recovery cursor (`recovery-cursor.ts`):** the cursor value now records the resolved database identity (`local:<dbPath>` / `remote:<host>:<dbPath>`). A cursor recorded against a different database no longer seeds `since_rowid`, and advance is monotonic only within the same database — so a `dbPath`/`remoteHost` change starts from the new DB's own startup watermark. This is cache-class state (rebuilds safely via GUID dedupe), so no migration is required.

## User Impact

- On no-SIP / AppleScript-only deployments, replies are delivered (unthreaded) instead of being silently dropped.
- Changing `dbPath` (or moving to/from a remote host) no longer wedges inbound message delivery; recovery resumes from the correct database.

## Evidence

**New/updated unit + integration tests — all green (90 passed across the 3 touched files):**

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.test.ts \
  extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts \
  extensions/imessage/src/monitor.last-route.test.ts
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  90 passed (90)
```

- `send.test.ts`: "resends unthreaded when the transport cannot deliver a threaded reply (#99638)" — asserts the first attempt carries `reply_to`, the retry drops it, the message is delivered, and the receipt reports no threaded reply.
- `recovery-cursor.test.ts`: cursor is scoped per (account, database), ignores a cursor from a different database, re-scopes on advance, adopts a pre-scoping legacy cursor once for the active database, and derives a stable identity across `dbPath`/`remoteHost`/custom `cliPath`.
- `monitor.last-route.test.ts`: existing downtime-recovery integration tests updated to the DB-scoped cursor and still passing.

Typecheck: `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` both clean.

Codex review (`autoreview`, gpt-5.5) run to clean: it flagged and I fixed upgrade-drop of legacy cursors, per-database cursor overwrite, custom-`cliPath` identity aliasing, and unthreaded-fallback receipt accuracy; final pass reports no actionable findings.

**Primary bug (#98835) verified live for context:** the same issue's primary conflict was verified end-to-end on a real two-Mac SSH deployment (gateway on one Mac driving `imsg` on another over an SSH wrapper) — three sequential multi-turn DMs all delivered replies with `outcome=completed` and zero `reply session initialization conflicted`. With this PR the remaining two reported items are addressed.
